_meta.title: Absence evidence — has each injured player's absence already been absorbed by his team's season stats?
_meta.why_this_matters: The line model uses season-to-date team ratings. Those ratings already exclude games a player missed. Deducting that player's production again double-counts. Only a NEW absence should move a projection.
_meta.method: For each player, the date of his most recent appearance is read from the 'Last 5 Games' table on his official NBA.com player page. Season per-game minutes and points are read from NBA.com per-game stats.

classification_rule.NEW_ABSENCE: last appeared 2026-11-10 or later — team stats do not yet contain a full game without him
classification_rule.ALREADY_BAKED_IN: last appeared 2026-11-09 or earlier — several team games have already happened without him
classification_rule.NOT_ABSENT: listed Available/Probable — expected to play, zero absence modelled
classification_rule.UNKNOWN: player page not captured — NOT inferred

_meta.coverage_note: Rows exist only where both the last-appearance date and (where needed) the season minutes were actually read from NBA.com. Players on the report without that evidence keep blank statistics and produce no adjustment.

verified_control_check.claim: his loss is real, not a rounding artefact
verified_control_check.observation: CLE net rating with him on the floor is +3.0 overall but -6.3 in losses; he played 33 minutes on 11/11. This is a genuine new absence.

_meta.retraction: An earlier revision of this file carried a row for Darius Garland (LAC) as a NEW_ABSENCE. He does not appear anywhere on the 11/13 official injury report — the LAC rows are Beal, Ingram, Martinelli, Miller and Niederhauser. The row was removed by scripts/verify_inline.py / verify_data.py cross-checking the evidence file against the report. It was an error, not an inference.
